status_summary: H.R. 2870, the Working Families Flexibility Act of 2025, was introduced on 2025-04-10. The House Education and Workforce Committee ordered it reported as amended on 2025-11-20 by a vote of 19 to 15 and reported it on 2026-02-12 (H. Rept. 119-496), placing it on the Union Calendar (No. 422). As reported, the compensatory time authority would last five years from enactment. The Senate companion, S. 1158, was introduced on 2025-03-26 and referred to committee. GovInfo bill status data record no floor vote on either bill.

timeline.event: S. 1158, the Senate Working Families Flexibility Act of 2025, was introduced and referred to the Senate Health, Education, Labor, and Pensions Committee; no later action is recorded.
H.R. 2870, the Working Families Flexibility Act of 2025, was introduced in the House.
The House Education and Workforce Committee ordered the bill reported as amended by a vote of 19 to 15.
The bill was reported with an amendment (H. Rept. 119-496) and placed on the Union Calendar (No. 422).

title: Allow private-sector employees to take compensatory time off in place of overtime pay
uncertainties: GovInfo bill status XML for H.R. 2870 and S. 1158 shows no action after 2026-02-12 and 2025-03-26 respectively; that data can lag congress.gov by days, which could not be opened. The bill as reported differs from the Mandate in limits it adds, including a five-year sunset, a 160-hour bank and a 1,000-hours-worked eligibility threshold.
